territory: Demo deployment three-layer write protection: src/lib/demo.ts, src/lib/demo-seed/** (seed.ts, content.ts, people.ts, photos.generated.ts), demo.test.mjs + content.test.mjs pins, IS_DEMO branches in src/proxy.ts, src/lib/auth.ts, src/lib/rate-limit.ts, src/lib/prisma.ts, src/lib/email.ts / email-queue.ts, src/app/api/demo/reset/route.ts, plus every demo-UI-reachable write path audited against the demoWriteAllowed allowlist (feed, catchups, profile letterhead, settings, collection, messages, support, notifications, uploads, onboarding). Spec: docs/spec/demo.md.

findings.title: Demo profile editing is broken: every contact-methods save and every admission-number save is refused by the write guard and surfaces as "That did not save. Check your connection."
findings.expected: docs/spec/demo.md's "They can" list promises demo visitors can "edit their own profile"; EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS in demo.ts explicitly allowlists displayEmail, instagram, linkedin, facebook, and links, so contact editing was clearly intended to work; the admission-number field on the letterhead should either save or show an honest demo message.
findings.actual: updateContactMethods ALWAYS includes `phone: phoneArr[0] ?? null, phones: ...` in its user.update data (profile-actions.ts:232-233), and neither "phone" nor "phones" is in EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS (demo.ts:120-147 — grep confirms zero mentions). isOwnProfileEdit (demo.ts:233-237) iterates every data key and returns false on the first non-allowlisted one, so the ENTIRE contact save (even one that only edits an Instagram handle) throws DemoWriteError. Same for updateProfileField("admissionNumber") — admissionNumber is in profile-actions.ts's own EDITABLE_FIELDS (line 53) but absent from demo.ts's list. The thrown error is caught by useAutoSave's bare `catch { failed = "That did not save. Check your connection." }` (pen.tsx:357-358), which per its own comment "stays put" as a persistent error state. The demo visitor's connection is fine; the message is false, and the demo looks broken on its flagship 'edit your profile' surface. Note /settings redirects to this letterhead (profile/[id]/page.tsx:353-356), so this is THE profile editor.
findings.evidence: demo.ts EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS (lines 120-147) lists name, bio, about, currentCity, secondaryCity, houses, displayEmail, birdOverride, avatarColor, workplace, jobTitle, instagram, linkedin, facebook, links, accountType, batchType, batchYear, yearJoined, yearLeft, gradeJoined, subjects, taughtFrom, taughtUntil, theme, updatedAt — no phone, phones, or admissionNumber. isOwnProfileEdit: `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(a.data)) { if (!EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS.has(key)) return false; ... }`. updateContactMethods: `await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: session.user.id }, data: { displayEmail..., phone: phoneArr[0] ?? null, phones: phoneArr.length > 0 ? JSON.stringify(phoneArr) : null, instagram..., links... } })` — the phone/phones keys are present on EVERY call regardless of what the visitor edited. updateProfileField case "admissionNumber" (profile-actions.ts:101-110) builds data.admissionNumber then `await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: session.user.id }, data })` (line 172) with no catch. Both are invoked from the letterhead commit handlers (letterhead-profile.tsx:397 `await updateProfileField(key, value)`, :425 `await updateContactMethods(rowsToPayload(contactRows))`) inside useAutoSave.run, whose catch shows "That did not save. Check your connection." The multi-phone columns landed 2026-07-30 (commit c5d826c), BEFORE the demo policy was written 2026-08-07 (0ea3174), so the allowlist was written against a stale field inventory; scripts/demo/verify-guard.mts only exercises `data: { bio: ... }` (line 83) so the wiring test never caught it.
findings.fixDirection: Either add "phone", "phones", "admissionNumber" to EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS in demo.ts (phone data on the invented persona is harmless and reset nightly), or make updateContactMethods omit the phone/phones keys when unchanged and give updateProfileField an IS_DEMO front door for admissionNumber. Additionally teach useAutoSave (or the action) to surface DemoWriteError's own message instead of blaming the connection: catch err, check `err.isDemoBlock` (or match the digest-safe way: return { error } from the action after catching DemoWriteError server-side, since thrown server-action errors are redacted in production).
findings.gateOrTest: Extend scripts/demo/verify-guard.mts with the REAL action payload shapes: a user.update carrying every key updateContactMethods and updateProfileField can emit, asserted allowed. Add a unit test in demo.test.mjs that asserts demoWriteAllowed("User","update",{where:{id:DEMO_USER_ID},data:{phone:null,phones:null,displayEmail:"x"}}) === true once fixed.
findings.reproPlan: Open the demo deployment, go to your own profile, click the pen, type anything into the contact block (e.g. an Instagram handle) and blur; observe the persistent "That did not save. Check your connection." Same with the admission number field. Writes touch only the disposable demo DB.

findings.title: "Start a Catch-up" is offered unconditionally in the demo but always fails with the generic "Something went wrong. Please try again." because Group/GroupMember creates are demo-denied
findings.expected: The demo either lets a visitor walk the Start-a-Catch-up flow to completion (the spec calls Catch-ups "the most interesting thing the site does and is worth letting people drive end to end"), or blocks the flow at its entrance with a purpose-written sentence like the eleven other front-doored actions (endCatchup and nudgeGroup in this very file have them).
findings.actual: The /catchups header renders an unconditional Canopy CTA "Start a Catch-up" linking to /catchups/new (catchups/page.tsx:266-275). The visitor names the Catch-up, picks up to 100 people, submits — and createCatchupWithPeople's transaction opens with `tx.group.create(...)` (actions.ts:442). "Group" and "GroupMember" are absent from ALLOWED_WRITE_MODELS (demo.ts:63-80: Post, Comment, Like, CommentLike, Bookmark, PollVote, PollOption, PhotoLove, Notification, UserPlace, Catchup*), so the extension throws DemoWriteError. runAction's catch (actions.ts:165-171) does not special-case isDemoBlock and returns `{ error: "Something went wrong. Please try again." }` — a message that invites retrying something that can never succeed, at the end of a multi-step form the visitor just filled in. The velvet-rope copy DemoWriteError carries ("This is a demo, so that one is switched off...") is discarded.
findings.evidence: demo.ts:63-80 ALLOWED_WRITE_MODELS has no "Group" or "GroupMember". actions.ts:441-450: `const catchupId = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { const group = await tx.group.create({ data: { name, visibility: "private", creatorId, members: { create: memberRows } }, ... }`. runAction:165-171: `catch (err) { if (isMissingCatchupTable(err)) {...} console.error("[catchups/actions]", err); return { error: "Something went wrong. Please try again." }; }`. grep of catchups/actions.ts shows IS_DEMO front doors only at lines 629 (endCatchup) and 1457 (nudgeGroup) — createCatchup and createCatchupWithPeople have none. catchups/page.tsx:266-274 renders the button with no demo gate: `<Link href="/catchups/new"><Button variant="primary"><Plus/>Start a Catch-up</Button></Link>`.
findings.fixDirection: Two options, either sufficient: (a) add Group and GroupMember to ALLOWED_WRITE_MODELS so demo visitors can genuinely start a Catch-up (the hidden Group container is harmless in a nightly-reset sandbox and lets people drive the feature end to end, matching the spec's stated intent), or (b) add an IS_DEMO front door at the top of createCatchup/createCatchupWithPeople with a purpose-written sentence, and hide or repurpose the /catchups CTA in demo. Also give runAction an `if ((err as {isDemoBlock?:boolean}).isDemoBlock) return { error: err.message }` branch so any future unnamed catch-up write shows the velvet rope instead of the generic failure.
findings.gateOrTest: demo.test.mjs: assert the decided policy (demoWriteAllowed("Group","create",{}) either true after (a), or a test that every exported catchups action names IS_DEMO before its first Group/GroupMember write). verify-guard.mts: attempt the createCatchupWithPeople write shape live.
findings.reproPlan: On the demo deployment: /catchups -> Start a Catch-up -> fill name, pick two people, submit. Observe the generic error. Demo DB only.

findings.title: Demo reset leaves the world half-written for its whole duration and can sign every concurrent visitor out to a dead /login page; nothing bounds two resets running at once, which can interleave and 500 or strip tables until the next reset
findings.expected: A reset pressed by one visitor (the Reset button is on every demo page, unauthenticated at the API) should not break another visitor's session or leave a corrupted world; ideally the rewrite is transactional or at least serialized.
findings.actual: Three connected defects. (1) seedDemo is ~40 sequential statements with no transaction (seed.ts:72-95 deletes 21 tables one by one, then recreates); for the several seconds it runs, concurrent visitors see an empty/partial feed, missing posts, and FK failures (P2003) on any in-flight comment/like against rows being deleted; a visitor's server action throws an unhandled Prisma error -> generic error UI. (2) In the window between `prisma.user.deleteMany({})` (seed.ts:95) and the user createMany (seed.ts:99), demoSession's findUnique on DEMO_USER_ID returns null (auth.ts:339-358 "if (!user) return null") and the (main) layout redirects that visitor to /login (layout.tsx:24-26) — a real credentials form on a deployment with no accounts and no way back except manually navigating away. (3) The 20s throttle is module state on ONE serverless instance ("serverless instances do not share memory... bounds one instance rather than the fleet", route.ts:35-42), and the cron GET path never touches lastReset at all — so two resets can genuinely run concurrently (two instances, or cron + button at 20:00 UTC). Both write the SAME fixed ids (demo-post-*, demo-u-*, demo-notif-*), so run B's createMany can hit P2002 against run A's rows and die mid-seed AFTER having deleted tables A had already filled — e.g. B's comment.deleteMany runs after A wrote comments, then B dies on post P2002: the demo serves a feed with zero comments until the next successful reset (nightly).
findings.evidence: seed.ts:66-71 comment admits the order is "spelled out so that a failure halfway through leaves a diagnosable state" — i.e. explicitly not atomic. route.ts:42-43: `const MIN_GAP_MS = 20_000; let lastReset = 0;` (module scope, per instance); GET handler (route.ts:86-112) has no throttle interaction. auth.ts:354-358: "An unseeded demo database is a deployment mistake... returning null sends the visitor to /login" — but the same null fires mid-reset, which is a routine nightly runtime state, not a deployment mistake. demo-bar.tsx:67-71 awaits the POST before navigating, so the presser is safe; every OTHER concurrent visitor is not. seedDemo's ids are deterministic constants (`pid = (slug) => \`demo-post-${slug}\``), so concurrent runs collide on primary keys by construction.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap seedDemo's body in one `prisma.$transaction` (a single-database rewrite of ~1,600 rows is well within Postgres limits; raise the interactive-transaction timeout for this call) so visitors read either the old world or the new, never the half-world, and the user row never vanishes; alternatively delete users LAST and upsert the visitor row first. Serialize resets with a Postgres advisory lock taken via the reset's own DIRECT client (it is its own session; do this on the unguarded client, not the pooled app client) or a cheap `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on a one-row lock table, so a second concurrent reset waits or no-ops. Consider `export const maxDuration = 60` on the route so a slow cold start cannot be killed mid-rewrite.
findings.gateOrTest: A demo-DB integration test (verify-guard style) that fires two seedDemo calls concurrently and asserts final counts equal one clean seed; and one that queries the demo mid-seed asserting the visitor row exists throughout (after the transactional fix, a concurrent read can never see it absent).
findings.reproPlan: Against the demo deployment: open two browsers, press Reset in one, navigate in the other within ~2s; observe the second browser bounced to /login or an empty feed. Concurrency half: fire two POST /api/demo/reset from two IPs in parallel and check the response of the loser plus post-state row counts. Demo DB only.

findings.title: The demo tells visitors to change their bird "from the species picker" while the species picker's only action refuses with "bird picking is switched off" — the spec-promised bird edit is impossible
findings.expected: docs/spec/demo.md "They can" list: "edit their own profile (including their bird)". demo.ts allowlists birdOverride in EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS (line 131), and updateAvatar's demo refusal actively directs the visitor: "The demo does not accept photo uploads, but you can change your bird from the species picker."
findings.actual: The only code path in the entire app that writes birdOverride is chooseBird (support/actions.ts:250 `data: { birdOverride: slug, birdPickedAt: new Date() }` — grep confirms no other writer), and chooseBird's second line is `if (IS_DEMO) return { error: "This is a demo, so bird picking is switched off." }` (line 202). So the demo (a) promises the capability in the spec, (b) allowlists the column for it, (c) tells the visitor where to go do it, and (d) refuses them when they get there. Even without the front door the write would fail anyway, because chooseBird also sets birdPickedAt, which is not in EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS. The /pick-bird page itself is supporter-gated (₹500 contribution), so a demo visitor most likely sees the payment-locked state — on a deployment where contributing is also blocked.
findings.evidence: settings/actions.ts:191: `if (IS_DEMO) return { error: "The demo does not accept photo uploads, but you can change your bird from the species picker." }`. support/actions.ts:199-202: `export async function chooseBird(slug: string)... if (IS_DEMO) return { error: "This is a demo, so bird picking is switched off." }`. Grep for birdOverride writers across src returns only support/actions.ts:250. demo.ts:131 includes "birdOverride" in EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS with header comment calling profile editing "a highlight of the product".
findings.fixDirection: Decide one way: (a) let the demo pick birds — in chooseBird, when IS_DEMO, skip the payment ledger (Contribution reads would find nothing anyway) and perform the update writing only birdOverride (drop birdPickedAt in demo, or add birdPickedAt to EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS), keeping the WEARABLE_SLUGS allowlist; this honors the spec sentence. Or (b) stop promising it: fix updateAvatar's demo copy and amend docs/spec/demo.md's "They can" line. Option (a) matches the demo's purpose (the aviary is a signature feature).
findings.gateOrTest: A demo.test.mjs case asserting the decided policy for the exact chooseBird write shape; a grep-style pin (like the closed-paths test) that the updateAvatar demo string does not reference a control that is itself demo-blocked.
findings.reproPlan: On the demo: profile -> pen -> tap the bird circle -> try to upload -> read the message directing you to the species picker -> go to /pick-bird -> observe locked/refused. Demo DB only.

findings.title: DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS blocks /onboarding but not /welcome, the real onboarding wizard, which renders fully in the demo and whose register step always fails on save
findings.expected: The spec closes onboarding because it is "not part of the product story": docs/spec/demo.md lists "/onboarding" among the routes a demo visitor cannot reach. The intent is that no onboarding wizard is reachable in the demo.
findings.actual: The live onboarding wizard is (main)/welcome, not (auth)/onboarding — welcome/page.tsx:13-18's own comment says (auth)/onboarding is "dead code today... post-registration hands off to this route instead". DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS (demo.ts:255-268, mirrored in proxy.ts:30-43) closes the dead route and leaves the live one open. The demo persona has admissionNumber null (the seed never sets it), so /welcome's already-onboarded guard does not bounce, and the full five-step wizard (welcome/register/houses/photo/done) renders to anyone who types the URL. Its register step calls saveOnboardingRegister, whose transaction writes `admissionNumber` on User (onboarding/actions.ts:82) — not in EDITABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS — so the save throws DemoWriteError and the whole step fails; the photo step is upload-blocked. An unlinked but guessable URL, so impact is bounded, but it is exactly the class of surface the closed-path list exists to keep out of a stranger's hands, and it is broken when found.
findings.evidence: demo.ts:255-268: DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS = ["/admin","/lab","/onboarding","/signup","/verify","/catchups/join","/forgot-password","/reset-password","/verify-email"] — no "/welcome". Route tree shows src/app/(main)/welcome/ and src/app/(auth)/onboarding/ both exist. welcome/page.tsx comment: "A small, unrelated 'complete your profile' page already lives at (auth)/onboarding (dead code today — it is not linked from anywhere post-registration hands off to this route instead)". onboarding/actions.ts:78-89: `await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { await tx.user.update({ where: { id: userId }, data: { admissionNumber: admissionNumber ?? null, workplace, jobTitle, subjects, currentCity: primaryLabel } }); ... })` — admissionNumber key always present. Seed user.createMany (seed.ts:99-137) sets no admissionNumber.
findings.fixDirection: Add "/welcome" to BOTH DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS lists (demo.ts and proxy.ts — the existing demo.test.mjs pin keeps them matched once both are edited). This is a two-line change; the register-step write failure then becomes unreachable.
findings.gateOrTest: demo.test.mjs already pins the two lists to each other; add a test asserting DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS covers every route-group directory whose purpose is account creation/onboarding (or at minimum a literal assertion that "/welcome" is present).
findings.reproPlan: Open <demo-host>/welcome directly: the wizard renders; complete the register step and observe the failure. Demo DB only.

findings.title: City autocomplete is dead throughout the demo (/api/places closed + empty gazetteer), so the promised "move their pins on the map" degrades to free-text entries that never gain coordinates and never appear on the map
findings.expected: docs/spec/demo.md promises visitors can "move their pins on the map". The demo policy even carves out raw queryRaw specifically so gazetteer pin-resolution keeps working (demo.ts:99-102). A visitor editing "Where you are" should get a working city picker, or at least cities that chart.
findings.actual: DEMO_CLOSED_APIS includes "/api/places" (proxy.ts:61-67, justified as "a metered geocoding provider... a billing amplifier" — a stale claim: the route now reads the repo's own 234k-row Place table via $queryRaw with no third party and is session-gated + rate-limited). Every LocationPicker keystroke gets a 403, the catch sets results to [] (location-picker.tsx:160-164), and the only option offered is the free-text row. A free-typed place saves with `lat: null, lng: null` (UserPlace writes are allowed), and pin resolution then has three chances: the stored coords (null), the small CITY_COORDS table, and the geocode.ts gazetteer fallback — which queries the demo's Place table, which is EMPTY (the demo setup in docs/spec/demo.md pushes schema + seedDemo only; scripts/dev/import-places.mjs is never run against it, and seed.ts never touches Place). So any city outside CITY_COORDS silently never appears on the map. The visible symptom: typing "Chennai" into the city editor offers no suggestions, only 'use exactly what you typed', and a typed "Lisbon" pin never shows — the picker and map look broken next to the real product.
findings.evidence: proxy.ts:61-67: `const DEMO_CLOSED_APIS = ["/api/upload","/api/razorpay","/api/auth","/api/places","/api/resend"]` with comment "/api/places -- a metered geocoding provider, i.e. a billing amplifier pointed at the owner's account." places/search/route.ts:104 shows the reality: `const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<PlaceRow[]>(Prisma.sql\`SELECT id, name, admin1, country, lat, lng FROM "Place" ...\`)` — local table, auth() + rateLimit("search") gated. location-picker.tsx:155-164: non-OK -> `Promise.reject` -> catch -> `setResults([])`; options then append `{ kind: "freeText", text: trimmed }` (line 202). demo.ts:99-102 keeps queryRaw open precisely for pin lookup: "without it every pin outside the small offline coordinate table vanishes" — but the demo Place table has no rows for it to find. seed-demo/seed.ts writes UserPlace coords only from CITY_COORDS (seed.ts:149-165).
findings.fixDirection: Remove "/api/places" from DEMO_CLOSED_APIS (the stated billing rationale no longer applies; the route is a gated read on own data, and the demo's rate limits being open is acceptable for a read the proxy could also cap), AND import the gazetteer into the demo database once (scripts/dev/import-places.mjs against .env.demo) so autocomplete and pin resolution work. If keeping it closed is preferred, hide the map-pin editing affordance in demo and amend the spec's "They can" list.
findings.gateOrTest: After reopening: a verify-guard.mts step that runs the picker's exact query shape against the demo DB and asserts >0 rows for "chennai"; a demo smoke assertion that a fresh UserPlace created via the picker carries non-null lat/lng.
findings.reproPlan: On the demo: profile pen -> Where you are -> type any city; observe no suggestions and (in devtools) the 403 from /api/places/search. Add "Lisbon", open /directory map, observe no pin. Demo DB only.

findings.title: DemoWriteError's visitor-facing message is unreachable dead copy: no action wrapper or client handler ever surfaces err.message, so layer 3 always presents as a broken site instead of a velvet rope
findings.expected: demo.ts:149-155 designs the error to be shown: "Carries a line fit to show a visitor: they should feel a velvet rope, not a stack trace" with default message "This is a demo, so that one is switched off. Everything else is yours to try."
findings.actual: Grep for isDemoBlock/DemoWriteError outside demo.ts/prisma.ts/tests returns ZERO handlers. Every reachable path either (a) catches generically and substitutes its own wrong message (runAction: "Something went wrong. Please try again."; useAutoSave: "That did not save. Check your connection."), or (b) lets the throw escape the server action, where production Next.js redacts thrown error messages to a digest, so the sentence cannot reach the client that way either. The backstop still blocks writes correctly (security is intact) — but its entire UX design ("for whatever nobody thought to name") silently degrades every future unnamed action into a broken-looking failure, which is exactly what happened with catch-up creation and the contact editor above.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "isDemoBlock\|DemoWriteError" src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v "lib/demo.ts\|lib/prisma.ts\|demo.test"` returns nothing. demo.ts:156-164 defines `readonly isDemoBlock = true` — a flag that exists to be checked and is checked nowhere in app code (only scripts/demo/verify-guard.mts:59 reads it, in tooling). Thrown server-action errors in production Next.js are replaced by a generic message + digest, so the constructor message is unreachable on the uncaught path by construction.
findings.fixDirection: Add one branch wherever actions funnel errors: in runAction (catchups), and as a small shared helper used by the letterhead/useAutoSave path and any other bare action: `if ((err as {isDemoBlock?: boolean})?.isDemoBlock) return { error: (err as Error).message }`. Server-side catching is required (client-side is impossible due to production redaction).
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test that runAction(() => { throw new DemoWriteError() }) resolves to { error: <the velvet-rope sentence> }.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (behavior fully determined by the quoted code; live proof duplicates findings 1-2).

findings.title: Shared demo persona turns concurrent visitors' like/vote toggles into unhandled P2002/P2025 throws (no unique-violation handler on any toggle)
findings.expected: With every demo visitor sharing DEMO_USER_ID (a documented trade), simultaneous toggles by two strangers are the demo's NORMAL concurrency, so the toggle actions need the P2002/P2025 tolerance the taxonomy asks for (the unique constraint is the guard; the code must absorb it firing).
findings.actual: toggleLike (actions.ts:477-494), toggleBookmark (:533-544), votePoll (:284-307) and toggleCommentLike are all check-then-write with no try/catch: two visitors hearting the same seeded post within the same second both read "no existing like", the second create hits the (userId, postId) unique index -> P2002 throws out of the action; two unhearting -> the second delete-by-id hits P2025. The client handler `const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) ...` (post-card.tsx:139-144) never sees a result — the promise rejects, leaving an unhandled rejection. State happens to converge (the desired end state already exists), so the visible cost is console errors/telemetry noise rather than wrong data, plus whatever the browser's unhandled-rejection surface shows. On the real deployment identities are distinct and this needs a double-click in one browser; on the demo it needs only two visitors, which is what a shared link produces.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:486-494: `if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId: session.user.id, postId } }); ... }` — no catch anywhere in the function; file-wide grep shows only 4 catch blocks, none in the toggles. Schema: Like @@unique(userId, postId) (schema.prisma:425-426 region). post-card.tsx handleLike has no try/catch.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap the create/delete pairs to treat P2002 on create and P2025 on delete as success (the desired state holds): a tiny shared helper `ignoreConstraintRace(err)` checking err.code in {"P2002","P2025"}. Benefits the real site's double-click case too.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit-level: call toggleLike twice concurrently against a test row and assert both resolve without throwing. Cheap deterministic version: assert the action resolves { success } when prisma throws a mocked P2002.
findings.reproPlan: Two browsers on the demo, heart the same seeded post within ~1s of each other; watch the second browser's console for the unhandled rejection. Demo DB only.

findings.title: Seeded demo notification hard-codes "open for answers until Friday" while the actual deadline is always reset-time + 4 days — wrong six days out of seven
findings.expected: Demo copy that names a deadline should agree with the deadline the same page's live countdown shows; the seed is rebuilt nightly, so relative wording ("open for four more days") stays true forever while a weekday name cannot.
findings.actual: seed.ts:447 writes the bell notification `"Round 2 of The 2010s, loosely is open for answers until Friday"`, while writeRound for round 2 (seed.ts:422-426) sets `answersCloseAt: daysAgo(-4)` — i.e. always 4 days after whatever day the reset ran. The nightly reset runs every day of the week, so the real close day is Friday only when the reset ran on a Monday. A visitor who clicks through sees a countdown disagreeing with the notification that brought them there — a small credibility crack in a surface whose entire job is polish.
findings.evidence: seed.ts:445-449: `{ type: "admin", message: "Round 2 of The 2010s, loosely is open for answers until Friday", link: "/catchups/demo-catchup", read: false, days: 2.4 }`; seed.ts:422-426: `await writeRound(CATCHUP_ROUND_2, 2, "answering", { questionsCloseAt: daysAgo(6), answersCloseAt: daysAgo(-4), publishAt: daysAgo(-5) });` with `daysAgo = (n) => new Date(Date.now() - n * 864e5)` (seed.ts:45).
findings.fixDirection: Reword to a relative phrase ("is open for answers for four more days") or compute the weekday at seed time from the same daysAgo(-4) date (IST formatting, since demo visitors are in India and the server runs UTC: use an explicit Asia/Kolkata formatter, not the server default).
findings.gateOrTest: content.test.mjs already lints seeded copy (em-dash test); add an assertion that no seeded notification message contains a weekday name.
findings.reproPlan: Open the demo bell on any day whose reset did not run on a Monday; compare with the round page countdown. Read-only.

verifiedClean: 6c proxy-vs-demo.ts closed-path drift: demo.test.mjs 'the closed-path list in proxy.ts matches the one in demo.ts' DOES compare both DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS lists fully (regex-extracts proxy's array, sorted deepEqual against demo.ts's export); the regex is currently robust (no quoted strings in comments inside the array, no nested '];'). DEMO_CLOSED_APIS has no counterpart in demo.ts so there is no second list to drift — single source. The lists themselves match verbatim today.
